summary: For this project, I explored the Dallol region in Ethiopia as a potential analogue for ancient Mars. I compared its mineral-rich landscape, volcanic activity, iron-bearing deposits, and evidence of water-related processes with conditions known to have existed on Mars billions of years ago. While Dallol differs from Mars in temperature and atmosphere, it shares several important geological characteristics, including extreme environmental conditions and mineral formations shaped by water. Studying locations like Dallol can help scientists better understand ancient Martian environments, improve exploration techniques, and identify places where evidence of past habitability may have been preserved.
details:
In this project I explored the Dallol region in Ethiopia as a analogue for ancient Mars. I compared its mineral-rich landscape, volcanic activity, and evidence of past water-related processes with similar features found on Mars. The goal was to identify an overlooked location that could help us better understand how geological and environmental conditions may have evolved on the Red Planet.

By studying places like Dallol, scientists can gain insights into mineral formation, planetary history, and the search for past habitable environments. The project was developed using publicly available NASA resources, scientific articles, and Microsoft PowerPoint.
